title: Mitigate fanout-oscillation and KV-cache coordination failures leading to burst tail spikes
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-02 we observed repeated capacity events and long-tail token latency for a subset of hosted inference pods. Root cause analysis shows a feedback loop between the continuous batcher’s fanout heuristic and the request affinity jitterer: the scheduler alternated between creating many small micro-batches and a few large batches ("fanout oscillation") which caused rapid KV-cache churn and bursty cold-KV misses. This amplified token latency spikes (p99->p999), caused unfairness across priority lanes, and led to transient capacity exhaustion on affected GPU nodes.

Impact: Several customers experienced elevated completion latency and a small number of API timeouts during a ~3 hour window. Incident triggered support escalations and one Dedicated customer reported degraded throughput.

Detection: Alerting was noisy initially; the first reliable signal was a new internal grafana panel showing batch-size distribution entropy rising above baseline (dashboard link below). Additional signals: per-cohort p95/p99 token latency divergence, KV eviction rate spike, and scheduler queue-length oscillation.

Root cause (summary): The continuous batcher uses a fanout heuristic that decides whether to route requests to multiple worker shards vs. saturate a single executor. A recent affinity-jitter change (ENG-137802) introduced randomized micro-shuffles to improve cache locality across long-lived streams. Under certain arrival patterns the jitterer and fanout heuristic interacted pathologically: the jitter caused request distribution to fluctuate, the fanout heuristic interpreted fluctuations as capacity imbalance and re-fanned requests, producing alternating bursts. These bursts increase effective working set churn in the KV cache (cache key residency oscillates), raising cold-KV misses and forcing recomputation/state syncs. The cache thrash plus bursty batch sizes produced long-tail service time.

Immediate mitigation applied (rolled within 90 minutes):
- Temporarily disabled the affinity jitterer for affected release channels (runtime-2.7) and reverted the jitter rollout flags. (owner: Liam O'Connor)
- Introduced a conservative circuit-breaker that enforces a max re-fan threshold per scheduling epoch (short term knob). (owner: Service Scheduling)
